Vehicle & Traffic Route Optimization Architecture

01 / NETWORK MODEL

Directed weighted transportation graph

The transportation network is modeled as a time-dependent directed graph whose route costs change with departure time and prevailing traffic.

JAIPUR → AJMER

Road graph on NH 48

Loading route map…

The graph is G = (V, E): V contains the depot and customer nodes, while E contains directed road segments. Node 0 is the single central depot; each customer i has demand qᵢ, service time sᵢ, and window [aᵢ, bᵢ]. Vehicles k ∈ K have capacity Qₖ.

xᵢⱼₖ = 1 if vehicle k travels directly from i to j; 0 otherwisetᵢₖ = departure time of vehicle k from node i
GRAPH ENTITIES

Route decision

  • Visit every customer exactly once
  • Start and return at depot 0
  • Respect Qₖ capacity and [aᵢ, bᵢ]
  • Minimize cost under traffic
DYNAMIC TRAFFIC MODEL

Edge cost changes with time

Cᵢⱼ(t) = clip(Bᵢⱼ + Aᵢⱼ sin(2πt/T + φᵢⱼ), 0, Cₘₐₓ)τᵢⱼ(t) = τ⁰ᵢⱼ (1 + αCᵢⱼ(t))

Bᵢⱼ is baseline congestion, Aᵢⱼ amplitude, φᵢⱼ phase, T the traffic period, and Cₘₐₓ the maximum congestion.

TEMPORAL PROPAGATION

Earlier edges affect later ones

For route (v₀, v₁, …, vₘ), arrivals and departures are propagated sequentially. Traffic encountered on an earlier edge changes the departure time and therefore the travel time of subsequent edges.

SCOPE & LIMITATIONS

Defined benchmark boundary

The benchmark uses synthetic networks, one depot, and deterministic traffic. It does not model stochastic accidents, weather, probabilistic forecasts, or multi-depot routing. If no direct edge exists, sparse-network waypoints may be connected through a shortest physical-distance path; traffic is evaluated on that path, but the path is not reoptimized by departure time.
